bibliography.title: A novel hybrid design and modelling of a customised graded Ti-6Al-4V porous hip implant to reduce stress-shielding: An experimental and numerical analysis
bibliography.authors: Naghavi SA, Tamaddon M, Garcia-Souto P, Moazen M, Taylor S, Hua J, Liu C.

study.research_problem: A solid Ti6Al4V hip stem is much stiffer than femoral bone, transfers load away from the proximal femur, and can drive stress shielding, bone resorption, aseptic loosening, and revision; porous stems lower stiffness and may support ingrowth but risk local weakness and fatigue failure.
study.exact_gap: Prior porous-stem studies often use a uniform lattice or an equivalent apparent modulus and do not resolve local strut stresses, stress shielding, and predicted bone resorption across all Gruen zones with an experimental FE check. A hybrid graded design therefore needs an explicit stiffness-strength-porosity trade-off and a direct fatigue boundary.
study.objective_or_hypothesis: Design a customized hybrid gyroid-diamond Ti6Al4V porous stem with a femoral-bone-like stiffness profile, at least 50% lattice porosity for osseointegration, and sufficient strength for 5 million cycles, and test whether it reduces stress shielding and modeled bone resorption relative to a solid stem of identical geometry.
study.study_design: A solid CNC Ti6Al4V stem and one SLM-manufactured hybrid porous stem were compared with an intact fourth-generation Sawbone femur. The porous stem combined solid neck/distal regions, 1-mm shells, D900 diamond lateral lattice (56.4% porosity), G1000 gyroid shaft (67.4%), and a stress-graded diamond medial region. A preliminary FE load of 4,839 N mapped local von Mises stress to 0.3-0.5 mm strut thickness. The paper says that a single Sawbone was used for each considered case (S004:C01) but later lists use of a single artificial femur as a limitation (S020:C01); retain this as one artificial-femur construct with unresolved per-case wording, not three independent Sawbones. Ten cortical rosette-gauge locations were used under stepped compression; CT-derived FE models were validated by stress-ratio trends and Bland-Altman analysis, then used for 2,300-N stress-shielding and Huiskes bone-resorption predictions, while 4,839 N was an additional stress/factor-of-safety load case. Stem stiffness was measured experimentally and by FE, and one porous stem underwent ISO 7206-4 cyclic testing to 5 million cycles or fracture.
study.sample_or_model: The artificial femur was 485 mm initially, trimmed to 408 mm and potted to a 328-mm working length; cortical E=16.7 GPa and cancellous E=0.155 GPa were assigned in FE. The source's per-case Sawbone wording is ambiguous against its explicit single-artificial-femur limitation (S004:C01; S020:C01), so n=1 artificial-femur construct must not be read as three independent femora. Five technical readings were collected at each 500-1,200 N experimental load step. The porous stem used Ti6Al4V grade 23 ELI powder (D10=21, D50=37, D90=51 micrometres), SLM 190 W/30-micrometre layers/1,000 mm/s/90-micrometre spot/85 J/mm3/110-micrometre hatch, heat treatment at 820 C for 120 min, sandblasting, and measured surface roughness 1.21+/-0.62 micrometres. FE assigned porous-stem E=95 GPa, solid-stem E=110 GPa, used C3D10 tetrahedra, 25 cortical mesh densities, and 2.4, 11.5, and 23.9 million elements for intact, solid, and porous models.
comparators: Intact Sawbone femur versus identical-geometry solid and hybrid porous stems
Experimental versus FE surface von Mises stress ratios at ten gauge locations
Porous versus solid stem SSI, stress ratio, and modeled bone resorption in Gruen zones 1-7
Experimental versus FE axial stiffness for solid and porous stems
Porous stem fixed in Sawbone versus fixed in PMMA/epoxy cement for FE safety factors
ISO 7206-4 target of 5,000,000 cycles and Ti6Al4V endurance limit of 375 MPa
method_spine: Construct a CAD stem customized to the large fourth-generation Sawbone and hybrid TPMS regions; map the preliminary 4,839-N FE strut stress field to graded medial-diamond thickness using region-specific nominal pore sizes/porosities, with the medial diamond varying across its graded thickness rather than preserving one uniform value.
Print the porous stem by SLM, heat-treat and sandblast it, characterize powder/roughness, and manufacture a solid Ti6Al4V control with the same outer geometry.
CT-scan and prepare one Sawbone, instrument ten identical cortical locations with rosette gauges, and collect stepped compression responses for intact, solid, and porous configurations.

Build intact and implanted Abaqus models with measured geometry, material assignments, contact/tie conditions, mesh convergence, and ISO-aligned boundary conditions; validate local stress ratios against gauges with Bland-Altman analysis.
Use the validated FE model to calculate Gruen-zone SSI and Huiskes strain-energy bone-resorption fractions at 2,300 N, then compare stiffness and yield/fatigue factors across daily activities.
Measure static stem stiffness and run one porous stem at 230-2,300 N and 5 Hz toward 5 million cycles, recording fracture location and cycle count.

verification: Twenty-five cortical mesh densities were tested and convergence was defined as <5% change after doubling element quantity; the final models used 2.4, 11.5, and 23.9 million elements (S009:C01).

The initial stress field under 4,839 N was used as a design/verification loop for assigning graded strut thickness, but no independent manufacturing or optimization verification is reported (S003:C01).
calibration: The porous-stem FE equivalent modulus (95 GPa) and other material properties were assigned from datasheets/literature rather than calibrated to the printed stem's complete local response (S009:C01).

The Huiskes dead-zone width s=0.6 came from prior two-year DEXA-based clinical densitometry and was applied to predict local bone loss; it was not calibrated with measurements from this experiment (S011:C01-S011:C02).

Thickness mapping uses von Mises stress bands from the preliminary model (0.3 mm at 0-40 MPa, graded 0.3-0.5 mm over 40-70 MPa, and 0.5 mm above 170 MPa); the 70-170 MPa interval is not specified in the text, and no sensitivity or optimization uncertainty is reported for these thresholds (S003:C01).
validation: Experimental and FE local cortical stresses had similar patterns; Bland-Altman analysis reported an approximately 4 MPa experimental-minus-FE bias with the plotted 95% limits and enabled additional FE scenarios (S014:C01).

The validation is local surface strain-gauge validation of a Sawbone construct, not validation of the full porous strut field, bone remodeling, interface micromotion, or a cadaver/clinical femur (S006:C01; S007:C01; S014:C01).
Static stiffness was measured for both stems and compared with FE, but only one specimen per stem was used and the paper emphasizes relative rather than absolute stiffness (S012:C01; S017:C01).
sensitivity: FE load cases span ISO 7206-4 (1,200 and 2,300 N), cycling, sitting, standing, walking, stance, stairs, and jogging up to 4,839 N; Sawbone and cement fixation were both examined for selected cases (S013:C01; S018:C01).

Gruen-zone SSI and resorption are spatially resolved, but no systematic sensitivity to porosity, strut thickness, contact gap, muscle forces, material anisotropy, or remodeling parameters is reported (S011:C01-S011:C02; S016:C01).
A single dynamic test supplies a failure boundary rather than a replicated fatigue sensitivity curve (S012:C01; S019:C01).
application_prediction: The predicted 70% SSI and 61% bone-loss reductions indicate a prototype-level application hypothesis; they do not establish reduced aseptic loosening, durable osseointegration, or a successful clinical replacement (S016:C01; S021:C01).
The authors' suggestion that bone ingrowth could improve in-vivo fatigue is explicitly speculative because no biological or orthotopic model was included (S019:C01).

primary_outcomes: The hybrid stem used D900 diamond lateral lattice (56.4% porosity), G1000 gyroid shaft (67.4%), a 300-500 micrometre stress-graded diamond medial region, and 1-mm shells; the grading was driven by the preliminary local stress field (S003:C01-S003:C02).

Bland-Altman comparison of ten gauge locations showed similar experimental/FE stress-ratio trends and an approximately 4 MPa experimental-minus-FE stress bias with nearly all points inside the plotted 95% limits; a geometry gap caused local M1 concentration and deviations (S014:C01).

At 2,300 N the porous stem produced more intact-like cortical stress/strain patterns. Total SSI was 32% for solid versus 10% for porous, a 70% reduction; SSI in Gruen zones 1, 6, and 7 changed from 69/45/68% to 34/12/40% (50%, 74%, and 41% reductions), while zone 4 showed little shielding in either stem (S015:C01; S016:C01).

The Huiskes model predicted total resorbed bone mass fractions of about 41% for solid and 16% for porous stems, corresponding to approximately 61% bone-loss reduction; the largest residual porous loss was proximal (especially zones 1 and 7), while zones 2, 5, and 6 showed roughly 86-97% reduction versus solid (S016:C01; S020:C01).

Experimental stiffness was 2.76 kN/mm for solid and 2.15 kN/mm for porous (22% lower); FE stiffness was 2.84 and 1.93 kN/mm. Both remained above the cited intact-human range of 1.16-1.45 kN/mm, although porous was closer (S017:C01).

At 2,300 N, maximum porous-stem stress was 112 MPa in Sawbone and 290 MPa in cement. Sawbone porous-section yield/fatigue FoS exceeded 8.1/3.9, with Goodman/Soderberg FoS 4.9/4.7; cement values were lower (yield/fatigue >6.2/2.9; Goodman/Soderberg 1.9/1.8). At the 4,839-N jogging load, the reported FoS were 3.3 yield, 1.6 fatigue, 2.3 Goodman, and 2.2 Soderberg (S018:C01).

The only dynamic porous-stem experiment fractured at the cement-pot restriction after 457,349 cycles, far below the 5,000,000-cycle ISO target; the failure directly limits the paper's infinite-service-life inference from static FE FoS (S019:C01; S020:C01; S021:C01).
study.highest_evidence_level_reached: Validated local stress-pattern comparison in a single artificial-femur construct plus nominal FE prediction of SSI/bone adaptation and static/fatigue safety, with one failed dynamic specimen; no replicated cadaver, biological osseointegration, interface micromotion, orthotopic, or clinical evidence.

argument_map.central_claim: A stress-graded hybrid gyroid-diamond porous Ti6Al4V stem shifts static cortical loading toward the intact-femur pattern and lowers model-predicted stress shielding and bone resorption relative to a solid control, but the prototype's single dynamic test fails before the 5-million-cycle target and its clinical replacement claim remains unvalidated.
data: The TPMS/strut-thickness design and as-built characterization define a physically manufacturable graded prototype (S003:C01-S003:C02).
Strain gauges and FE show similar local stress-ratio trends, with a quantified Bland-Altman bias and a documented geometry-gap exception (S006:C01; S014:C01).
Gruen-zone FE outcomes show lower SSI and modeled resorption with porous versus solid stems, while stiffness is reduced but still above the cited intact range (S015:C01-S017:C01).
Static FoS calculations appear favorable, but one dynamic test fractures at 457,349 cycles versus the 5,000,000-cycle target (S018:C01-S019:C01).
argument_map.warrant: A lower-stiffness, spatially graded stem can plausibly reduce stress transfer mismatch only when local stress redistribution, mechanical strength, and fatigue are evaluated together; a predicted remodeling proxy cannot override an observed device-level fatigue failure.
backing: The solid comparator shares the stem geometry and the intact/solid/porous constructs share the mounting and stepped-load framework, improving relative comparison fairness (S004:C01; S007:C01).
Mesh convergence, local strain-gauge comparison, and Bland-Altman analysis provide a traceable FE validation layer before application predictions (S009:C01; S010:C01; S014:C01).
The analysis retains regional Gruen-zone differences rather than reporting only a whole-femur average (S011:C01-S011:C02; S016:C01).
argument_map.qualifier: The stress-shielding and bone-loss reductions apply to the stated Sawbone geometry, potting, simplified loading, material laws, contact assumptions, and Huiskes remodeling parameters.
rebuttals_or_boundaries: The 457,349-cycle fracture limits a broad infinite-service-life interpretation from static FE safety factors and shows that potting/interface failure is a critical boundary; because the dynamic test used PMMA cement while many >2 Goodman/Soderberg values were for Sawbone, this is not a direct same-condition contradiction (S012:C01; S018:C01-S020:C01).
FE validation uses local cortical surface strains, not the porous strut stresses, interface micromotion, or cadaveric bone under physiologic muscle loads (S014:C01; S020:C01).
The predicted bone-resorption fraction is a mechanobiological model output, not a measured DEXA, histological, or clinical bone-loss endpoint (S011:C01; S016:C01).
One solid stem, one porous stem, and an ambiguously reused/single artificial-femur construct do not quantify manufacturing, anatomical, or fatigue variability (S004:C01; S020:C01).

measured: Powder composition and printing parameters are reported manufacturing inputs (not outcome measurements); measured outputs include surface roughness, load-displacement stiffness, cortical rosette-gauge strain/stress, and one porous-stem dynamic fracture cycle count (S003:C02; S006:C01; S007:C01; S017:C01; S019:C01).
Experimental versus FE local stress-ratio comparisons and Bland-Altman bias/limits (S014:C01).
predicted: FE strut/cortical von Mises stress, strain, yield/fatigue/Goodman/Soderberg FoS, Gruen-zone SSI, and Huiskes resorbed mass fractions (S011:C01-S013:C01; S015:C01-S018:C01).
inferred: Lower porous-stem SSI and more intact-like strain indicate a lower risk of stress shielding under the modeled 2,300-N loading (S015:C01-S016:C01).
A porous stem closer to intact-femur stiffness may preserve a more physiological mechanical stimulus, but both tested stems remain stiffer than the cited intact human range (S017:C01).

Potential improved fixation or reduced aseptic loosening are application hypotheses downstream of stress/remodeling proxies, not measured or directly predicted endpoints (S001:C01; S020:C01; S021:C01).
Bone ingrowth could improve fatigue in vivo is an author hypothesis, not a tested biological mechanism (S019:C01).
recommended: Repeat static and fatigue testing over multiple printed stems and femora, include cadaveric or subject-specific bones, physiological muscle/contact loads, and quantify AM geometry variability.
Measure implant-bone shear, micromotion, contact coverage, and biological osseointegration; use DIC or full-field methods to complement local strain gauges.
Re-optimize the lattice after the observed potting/interface fracture and test to the complete ISO 7206-4 five-million-cycle requirement before replacement claims.
proxy_to_outcome_bridges: FE SSI and Huiskes resorbed mass fraction are model proxies, not measured DEXA bone mineral density, histology, fixation, or aseptic-loosening outcomes.
Sawbone cortical surface strain validates selected local stress trends, not human bone remodeling, porous strut strength, or stem-bone micromotion.
Static yield/fatigue FoS and Goodman/Soderberg predictions do not substitute for replicated cyclic device testing; the observed 457,349-cycle fracture is the relevant boundary.
Porosity and surface roughness indicate design intent for ingrowth but are not evidence that bone actually invaded or bonded to the lattice.
overclaim_risks: The abstract/conclusion presents approximately 60-70% reduction in bone loss/SSI as a long-term implant benefit although both are FE predictions and the experiment used a single Sawbone (S016:C01; S021:C01).

Static FoS values are described as implying infinite service life even though the only PMMA-cement dynamic specimen failed at about 9% of the 5-million-cycle target; static Sawbone and cement FoS are not interchangeable conditions (S012:C01; S018:C01-S019:C01).
The phrase 'potential replacement for the generic solid implant' exceeds the artificial-femur, simplified-loading, single-specimen, and failed-fatigue evidence boundary (S001:C01; S021:C01).
The bone-ingrowth rationale is not tested by histology, imaging, animal, or implant-interface mechanics, and the stem remained stiffer than the cited intact femur range (S003:C01; S017:C01).

section_moves.move: Make stress-driven grading reproducible and distinguish nominal from as-built geometry
section_moves.execution: The workflow first models a uniform hybrid stem, exports local von Mises stress, maps stress bands to strut thickness, then prints, heat-treats, sandblasts, and measures roughness; it also records the CAD-to-femur contact gap (S003:C01-S003:C02; S014:C01).
section_moves.transferable_principle: For a graded AM implant, report the optimization field, threshold map, process state, and as-built deviations as separate states so readers can follow what was designed, manufactured, and actually modeled.
section_moves.failure_mode: Treating a nominal stress-based thickness map as equivalent to the printed local strut geometry hides process defects and contact mismatch that can dominate fatigue.

section_moves.move: Validate the FE model locally before escalating to whole-zone predictions
section_moves.execution: The study compares ten matched strain-gauge locations with FE stress ratios, quantifies Bland-Altman bias, explains the M1 discrepancy through a contact gap, and only then predicts Gruen-zone SSI and Huiskes resorption at 2,300 N; 4,839 N is used for an additional stress/factor-of-safety case, not for the SSI/resorption endpoint (S006:C01; S010:C01; S014:C01; S016:C01; S018:C01).
section_moves.transferable_principle: Use a transparent local validation layer with agreement statistics and named outliers before applying a model to unmeasured regions or biological proxies.
section_moves.failure_mode: A few matching surface gauges cannot validate strut-level stresses, interface micromotion, or bone-remodeling predictions; the validated domain must be stated explicitly.

section_moves.move: Place static predictions and fatigue failure on one evidence ladder
section_moves.execution: The paper reports favorable static FoS and modeled SSI, then discloses that the porous stem fractured after 457,349 cycles in the PMMA-cement dynamic setup; the discussion recognizes this as a major drawback, while static Sawbone and cement FoS must remain condition-specific (S012:C01; S018:C01-S020:C01).
section_moves.transferable_principle: When a device-level durability test and static model use different fixtures or fixation states, lead with the observed failure, preserve the condition mismatch, and downgrade service-life or replacement language accordingly.
section_moves.failure_mode: Letting static FoS or a predicted infinite life dominate the narrative can erase the most decision-relevant negative result.

author_reported: FE validation used a fourth-generation artificial Sawbone rather than cadaveric femur; vertical flat loading omitted muscle forces and soft tissues (S020:C01).
Strain gauges measured only local cortical surface microstrain; DIC was suggested as an alternative whole-field method (S007:C01; S020:C01).
Manufacturing precision produced a stem-femur geometry gap and local force concentration; interface shear stress and micromotion were not examined (S014:C01; S020:C01).
Only one artificial femur and one solid/porous stem were manufactured, so stiffness and fatigue measurements were single-specimen outcomes (S020:C01).
reader_identified: Five technical readings at each load step are repeated measurements on one construct, not independent biological or manufacturing replicates; no confidence intervals for stiffness, SSI, or fatigue are reported.

One dynamic specimen was tested in PMMA cement and fractured at the potting restriction; static FoS were reported separately for Sawbone and cement, so the result cannot separate lattice fatigue from cement/potting/interface failure, align a single condition with every static FoS, or estimate a population fatigue distribution (S012:C01; S018:C01; S019:C01).

The FE porous-stem material is a homogeneous equivalent E=95 GPa despite the paper's motivation to resolve local lattice stresses; local strut/contact mechanics are therefore incompletely represented.
Tied contacts, epoxy-filled gaps, simplified isotropic materials, and ISO vertical loads can alter force transfer and micromotion relative to an uncemented or physiologically loaded hip.
The Huiskes dead-zone parameter and resorption model are imported from prior work, only the bone-loss branch is evaluated, and no DEXA/histology/in-vivo remodeling validation is included.
A minimum porosity is justified as favorable for osseointegration, but no cells, animal tissue, bone ingrowth, or interface bonding endpoint is measured.
The stress-thickness optimization is based on a single preliminary load case and lacks uncertainty or multi-load robust optimization.
likely_bias_direction: The solid/porous comparison on one Sawbone and matched outer geometry improves internal fairness but may overfit a single anatomy and potting condition.

Gaps and loose distal contact likely concentrate load at proximal gauge M1 and can bias local validation and predicted zone shielding; tied interfaces elsewhere may simultaneously understate micromotion.
Using equivalent homogeneous porous properties and a dead-zone remodeling model may smooth local failures and overstate the generality of predicted bone-loss reduction.

Selecting favorable static FoS and modeled SSI before the single negative fatigue result can bias the translational narrative toward efficacy; the PMMA dynamic fixture and Sawbone-versus-cement static cases also limit direct condition matching (S012:C01; S018:C01-S020:C01).
limitations.scope_boundary: The study supports a manufacturable hybrid-stem design workflow, relative static stress redistribution, and model-based Gruen-zone predictions in one artificial-femur construct. It does not demonstrate replicated fatigue durability, osseointegration, interface fixation/micromotion control, measured bone preservation, or clinical replacement of a solid hip stem.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Write a graded-implant optimization loop as a chain from preliminary local stress field to thickness map, print state, as-built deviation, and independently tested outcome.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Methods design rationale, manufacturability reporting, and audit of nominal-to-as-built transfer.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: A single stress-mapped design load and one printed specimen do not establish robust optimization across activity, anatomy, process, or fatigue variability.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Use local strain-gauge agreement statistics and named geometry-driven outliers to bound what an FE validation actually supports before applying it to spatial remodeling predictions.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: FE validation Results, uncertainty paragraph, and Discussion evidence boundary.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: Agreement at ten cortical surface points does not validate porous strut stresses, interface micromotion, or biological remodeling, especially when M1 shows a contact-gap exception.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Keep static safety-factor predictions, modeled biological proxies, and observed cyclic failure in separate evidence lanes, letting the failure define the service-life boundary.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Results synthesis, Discussion, conclusion proportionality, and design-go/no-go decisions.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: The single dynamic test used PMMA cement and fractured at 457,349 cycles; many >2 Goodman/Soderberg FoS values were for Sawbone, while the 2,300-N cement values were 1.89/1.82, so the failure bounds device durability without being a same-condition contradiction to every static prediction (S012:C01; S018:C01; S019:C01).

critical_weaknesses: Single Sawbone and single stems provide no independent variability estimate.
Local strain-gauge validation does not cover porous struts, interface micromotion, or biological bone adaptation.

Static FE service-life predictions are not established by the single PMMA-cement dynamic specimen, which fractured at 457,349 cycles far below the ISO 5-million-cycle target; fixture and Sawbone-versus-cement condition mismatch remain unresolved.
Predicted SSI/bone-loss reductions are not measured bone-preservation or clinical loosening outcomes.

summary_zh: 这篇研究把定制化混合 Gyroid-Diamond TPMS、应力驱动支杆厚度梯度、Sawbone 应变片和 FE Gruen 区域预测串成一条设计-验证链。相同外形的实心/多孔柄比较显示，多孔柄总应力遮挡指数从 32% 降到 10%，Huiskes 模型预测骨吸收从 41% 降到 16%，实验刚度从 2.76 降到 2.15 kN/mm；但两者仍高于引用的人体完整股骨刚度范围。FE 与十个皮质表面测点趋势一致，Bland-Altman 给出约 4 MPa 偏差，但 M1 的几何间隙造成了局部载荷集中。更关键的是，静态 FoS/Goodman/Soderberg 推出“无限寿命”的同时，唯一动态试样在 457,349 次就从水泥罐限制段断裂，远低于 ISO 7206-4 的 500 万次。因此可迁移的写作能力是：把名义设计→打印状态→局部验证→区域代理→器械疲劳分层，并让实际失败结果定义服务寿命边界；不能把预测骨量保存或短期静态安全写成临床替代证据。
reader_notes: Primary Codex reader reviewed all 25 non-reference packet chunks in exact heading order: S001:C01, S002:C01-S002:C03, S003:C01-S003:C02, S004:C01-S021:C01, including both chunks of S011.
The article is original mixed experimental/FE implant research, not an in-vivo animal or clinical study despite cue fields that list in_vivo_animal and in_vitro.

The strongest validation is local cortical surface stress agreement in one artificial femur; the porous strut field, interface micromotion, remodeling, osseointegration, and clinical outcomes remain outside the validated domain.
The observed 457,349-cycle fracture is retained as a decisive negative result and is not reconciled away by the static FE safety-factor inference.
S004:C01's per-case Sawbone wording conflicts with S020:C01's single-artificial-femur limitation; the card preserves this ambiguity and does not treat the configurations as three independent femora.

The dynamic PMMA-cement fixture, static Sawbone cases, and static cement case have distinct conditions; the fracture bounds durability but is not a same-condition contradiction to every static FoS value (S012:C01; S018:C01-S019:C01).
